motivating_failure: A 50% rank-reversal probability is expected even when independent traits evolve under the same stochastic Brownian process; observed differences in estimator strength can also arise from phylogenetic geometry.

population.source: AusTraits 7.0.0 qualified positive-numeric log-core and its exact source-native trees

process_null.simulated_independent_trait_evolution: Brownian motion sigma2=1 on each exact system tree, starting at root value 0
process_null.species_state_values: all new simulations; no observed trait states used in the null except to verify exact tree and K identity
process_null.independence: separate Brownian draws for every trait system and simulation replicate, conditional on each exact input phylogeny
process_null.expectation: Same process parameter across all named traits and families; observed tree shape and taxon coverage can nevertheless induce systematic differences in K distributions.
process_null.simulation_metric: exact phytools phylosig-method-K formula evaluated using an O(n_edges) phylogenetic independent-contrasts recursion, checked against phytools on observed trait states before opening null result

measures: held-out-family absolute log(K) prediction gain versus held-out-family global-mean baseline
held-out-family within-family rank prediction gain versus 0.5 baseline
weighted cross-family pair-order reversal for trait pairs co-occurring in >=10 families
conditional family repeatability from log(K) ~ 0+named_trait+(1|family), REML
analysis.empirical_tail_p: (1 + #{null replicate >= observed})/(1+valid replicates) for predictability and repeatability; two-tailed rank reversal assessment and null interval
analysis.note: 64 Monte Carlo replicates resolve p-values no smaller than 1/65 and are preliminary process-null calibration; increase precision without changing specification only if warranted.

interpretation.null_emulates_empirical_structure: If the observed family or trait effects lie inside the identical-process null distribution, do not attribute them to process heterogeneity.
interpretation.beyond_null: If observed family repeatability and trait ranking exceed calibrated null tails on both tree axes, infer evidence of reproducible heterogeneity in the phylogenetic-signal statistic beyond equal-rate Brownian processes, not necessarily selection/adaptation.
interpretation.observed_reversal_near_half: Do not treat 50% reversal itself as evidence of biological rewiring.

limitations: Different traits use independently generated Brownian trajectories, so cross-trait evolutionary covariance is absent from this null.
Underlying published phylogenies and taxonomy are assumed correct.
This is a post-outcome test, not a revision of the pre-frozen rho programme.
No mechanistic inference from a single equal-rate-Brownian null.
